meanings.note: After a noun, means 'one' (إشي واحد، سؤال واحد، إيد واحدة); with الـ (الواحد) it is the everyday impersonal subject 'a person / one'.

examples.trans: A person has to tell the truth.
I have just one question.

meanings.note: Followed directly by a subjunctive verb: بيقدر يتحمل ('can endure'), بتقدري تاخدي ('you can take').

examples.trans: You can sit here.
I couldn't sleep yesterday.

meanings.note: Covers enduring mistreatment (يتحمل الظلم) and taking responsibility (نتحمل المسؤولية).

examples.text: ما بقدر أتحمل أكتر من هيك.
examples.trans: I can't put up with more than this.
We must take responsibility.

meanings.note: Central theme word of the show: يتحمل الظلم ('endure unfairness') and ظلمهم ('their mistreatment').

examples.trans: Injustice is hard for a person to bear.
We won't accept unfairness.

meanings.note: لمرحلة معينة means 'up to a certain point / stage'.

examples.trans: We reached a difficult stage.
High school is a very important stage.

meanings.note: Follows an indefinite noun to mean 'a certain / particular' (لمرحلة معينة 'up to a certain point').

examples.trans: Do you have a specific time we can meet?
Is there a particular reason for your question?

meanings.note: Used in farewells (أشوفك بعدين! 'See you later!') and narratives (وبعدين 'and after that').

examples.trans: We'll talk about it later.
See you later, Mariam!

meanings.note: Vivid Jordanian verb for losing patience after holding frustration inside (الواحد بيفقع 'a person snaps/bursts').

examples.trans: I'm going to burst from this unfairness.
I burst out laughing at the joke.

meanings.note: Negates past and b-present verbs (ما إجيت، ما بعرف) and idioms like ما عليكم ('never mind'); after قبل or بدل (قبل ما، بدل ما) it links a verb clause.

examples.trans: I didn't hear the bell.
Come before the school closes.

meanings.note: Imperative feminine اسكتي ('be quiet!'); ما رح نسكت means 'we won't stay silent'.

examples.trans: Everyone fell silent when the principal entered.
We won't stay quiet about our right.

meanings.note: Spoken feminine singular 'you', spelled with final ي to reflect the Jordanian pronunciation inti.

examples.trans: Are you a new girl here?
What do you think?

meanings.note: Primary spoken verb for 'see' across the Levant, also used in farewells like أشوفك بكرة! ('See you tomorrow!') and نشوفك! ('See you!').

examples.trans: I saw everything with my own eyes.
See you tomorrow morning!

meanings.note: Core Levantine question word for 'what?' (شو صار؟) and casual conversation starter ('So, ...').

examples.trans: What are you doing here?
So, ready to go?

meanings.note: Two essential senses: 'happen' (اللي صار 'what happened') and 'become / turn into' (صارت كابوس، صار الوقت).

examples.trans: Tell me what happened exactly.
It's time we head to class.

meanings.note: At AlRawabi, الساحة is the central open courtyard where students gather.

examples.trans: We went down to the courtyard at recess.
The girls are standing in the middle of the courtyard.

meanings.note: Past tense linking verb (كنت، كنتي، كان، كنا) and subjunctive تكون / نكون ('to be'); ما كان عندي means 'I didn't have'.

examples.trans: I was at school in the morning.
Today was very long.

meanings.note: Points to a place away from the speaker or back to the scene of an event (كنتي هناك 'you were there').

examples.trans: Look over there by the tree.
We have to be there on time.

meanings.note: The main Levantine verb for 'talk / say / tell', far more common in Amman than تكلم.

examples.trans: Who told you the news?
Tell me what happened with you.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine dative base taking pronoun endings: إلي (to me), إلك (to you), إلها (to her), إلنا (for us), إلهم (to them).

examples.trans: This book is for you.
Tell me the truth.

meanings.note: Definite الحقيقة refers to what actually happened behind appearances.

examples.trans: Everyone must know the truth.
The truth will come out soon.

meanings.note: Core Levantine verb for 'come': past إجيت / إجت, b-present باجي / بتيجي.

examples.trans: Why didn't you come yesterday?
Next time I'll come with you.

meanings.note: Expresses location (عند باب الساحة), movement toward someone with لـ (لعندي 'up to me'), and possession (عندي وقت 'I have time', عنا 'we have').

examples.trans: I have class right now.
Come over to me for a moment.

meanings.note: With object suffix مسكتني ('she grabbed me').

examples.trans: She held my hand and we walked together.
Layan grabbed me by my shoulder.

meanings.note: With بـ + الـ, بالقوة means 'by force / forcefully'.

examples.trans: She grabbed my hand forcefully.
Honesty gives us strength.

meanings.note: Answers a question negatively ('no') or forms negative commands before a second-person subjunctive verb (لا تصدقوها! 'don't believe her!').

examples.trans: No Miss, that's not true.
Don't worry, everything is fine.

meanings.note: Form II verb (saddaq, written here with shadda to distinguish it from the noun صدق 'honesty'): أصدقك ('believe you'), لا تصدقوها ('don't believe her').

examples.trans: You have to believe me, Miss.
Nobody believed her lie.

meanings.note: Placed before a b-present verb (عم بكذبوا، عم بتتحديني) to spotlight an action happening right now.

examples.trans: The girls are studying in the library right now.
What are you saying?

meanings.note: Construes with على for lying to or about someone (كذبوا علي، عم بكذبوا عليكي).

examples.trans: I have never lied to you.
The girls are lying to the principal.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine indefinite person word; ما حدا means 'nobody'.

examples.trans: Is anyone in the classroom?
Nobody believed me.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian/Levantine word for 'here' (formal هنا).

examples.trans: Come sit here next to me.
Life is very sweet here.

meanings.note: Literally 'play', and idiomatically ما حدا بيلعب معها / معي ('nobody messes with her / me').

examples.trans: We played ball in the courtyard.
Don't play this game with me.

meanings.note: Takes suffixes معي (with me), معك (with you), معها (with her), معنا (with us), معكم (with you all), معهم (with them), and forms مع السلامة! ('Goodbye!').

examples.trans: Come sit with us.
Goodbye, see you tomorrow!

meanings.note: Central setting: مدرسة الروابي للبنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls').

examples.trans: The school is close to our house.
I like going to school early.

meanings.note: Independent first-person singular pronoun for any gender.

examples.trans: I am a student at the school.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun, كل means 'every' (كل يوم، كل إشي); with الـ (الكل) it means 'everyone'; with suffixes (كلنا، كلهم، كلها) 'all of us/them/it'.

examples.trans: Everyone knows the story.
We see each other every day.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian word corresponding to formal شيء; definite form الإشي, plural أشياء.

examples.trans: There is something important I want to say.
Nothing happened.

meanings.note: Idiomatic in شفت بعيني / بعينها ('saw with my/her own eyes') and بتشوفه العين ('the eye sees').

examples.trans: I saw what happened with my own eyes.

examples.text: مش كل إشي بتشوفه العين صح.
examples.trans: Not everything the eye sees is true.

meanings.note: Placed before a name or title whenever addressing someone directly (يا دينا، يا مس فاتن); natural English usually drops it.

examples.trans: Come here, Mariam.
Thank you very much, Miss.

meanings.note: Singular بنت, definite البنت, plural بنات / البنات ('AlRawabi School for Girls' = مدرسة الروابي للبنات).

examples.trans: She is a very bright girl.
The girls are standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Pronounced jdiid / jdiide in Jordanian speech (بنت جديدة 'a new girl').

examples.trans: Noaf is a new student at school.
I have a new notebook.

meanings.note: In the past مع ما (ما عرفت شو أعمل), means 'I didn't know what to do'; b-present بعرف means 'I know'.

examples.trans: I know this place well.
I didn't know how to answer the question.

meanings.note: Core Levantine word (mniih) used adverbially after verbs of knowing or listening: عارفة منيح ('know very well'), اسمعي منيح ('listen well').

examples.trans: Listen to me well, Noaf.
I know the story well.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine word for 'who?' in both direct and indirect questions (مين حكى إلك؟، بعرف مين عم بيحكي).

examples.trans: Who is standing at the door?
I don't know who took the pen.

meanings.note: Both the moral virtue 'honesty' and 'the truth' when speaking (بحكي الصدق).

examples.trans: Honesty is among the most important values.
I am telling the truth.

meanings.note: Negates nouns, adjectives, participles, prepositional phrases, and لازم (مش صح، مش معنا، مش قادرة، مش بعد اليوم).

examples.trans: This talk is not true.
I'm not upset with you.

meanings.note: Besides 'he/it', separates a definite subject from a definite predicate to mean 'is' (مش كل إشي بتشوفه العين هو الحقيقة).

examples.trans: Honesty is the most important thing.
Where is the notebook?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian pronoun corresponding to formal نحن.

examples.trans: We have been friends for a long time.
Come sit with us.

meanings.note: Standard Levantine future marker placed before a bare subjunctive verb (رح أخلص، ما رح نسكت).

examples.trans: I'm going to tell the truth.
I won't forget this day.

meanings.note: Temporal preposition: مش بعد اليوم ('not after today') and بعد هيك ('after this').

examples.trans: We'll see you after class.
I won't stay quiet after today.

meanings.note: Indefinite كل يوم means 'every day'; definite اليوم means 'today' (مش بعد اليوم 'not after today').

examples.trans: We see each other every day at school.
Today the weather is very pleasant.

meanings.note: In أشوفك قريب! ('See you soon!'), used temporally for 'before long'.

examples.trans: We'll meet soon.
See you soon, my friend!
